criteria.note: No literal credential, API key, token or password is introduced. .mcp.json carries only a public static OAuth client_id ('helix-local-mcp-agent') and a solution-id header value, neither of which is a secret; config.json and both rubrics contain only thresholds and prose. D7's collector deliberately records detect-secrets' hashed_secret truncated to 32 chars (static_evals.py) rather than any raw value, so no credential reaches the evidence files either.

Nothing in the diff logs imagery, biometrics or PII. The diagnostics added by static_evals.py and run_evals.py emit only gate names, rule ids, repo-relative file paths, counts and truncated tool messages; the judge payloads record criterion ids, scores and citations. No frame buffer, landmark array or face geometry is touched. The audit markdown names GitHub account handles and the operator email, which are the audit trail's own required identity fields, not incidental logging of user data.

Both entry points validate their untrusted inputs before use: _safe_key() (run_evals.py, static_evals.py) constrains the EVAL_KEY environment variable to a single anchored path segment and rejects '.'/'..' before it is joined into a written path, and _validated_thresholds() checks every config-supplied numeric threshold for type (rejecting bool) and for range against an explicit per-key interval, plus the list type of disallowedLicenses, before any of them decides a pass/fail. The judge response is likewise validated: missing criterion ids, sub-1.0 scores without a citation, and unparseable JSON all raise rather than being consumed.

No bare except and no unbounded retry. Collectors catch json.JSONDecodeError narrowly and return the raw tool output as evidence instead of swallowing it; the judge retry loop is a fixed two-attempt 'for attempt in (1, 2)' that raises SystemExit with the last error rather than looping or degrading to N/A; the git worktree is removed in a finally block; verdict() raises SystemExit for an unknown gate instead of defaulting to PASS. The broad 'except Exception' in score_rubric captures the message into last_err, writes the raw response to evidence, and surfaces it on exhaustion, so nothing is silently discarded. Error text is written to local evidence files for the operator, not returned to an untrusted consumer.

The diff adds no dependency manifest entry at all - no requirements.txt, pyproject.toml, package.json or lockfile change appears. The new Python modules import only stdlib (json, os, re, shutil, subprocess, sys, tempfile, pathlib) and shell out to already-installed tools. With no dependency added, the criterion cannot be exercised by this diff.

The one place external input reaches a path is EVAL_KEY, and it is contained before use: _safe_key() requires a full match of [A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63} - a character class that admits no '/' or '\\' - and additionally rejects '.' and '..', so the join into ROOT/.spec/aire-docs/.../eval-evidence/<key> cannot escape that root. Every other path is built from the ROOT constant resolved from __file__ plus literal segments; the base ref from argv is passed to git as an argument, not joined into a filesystem path; and the temp prompt file uses tempfile.NamedTemporaryFile with an unlinking finally.
